decision: Team of five: Harshit, Michael, Vlad, Ishita, Youssouf
rationale: Formed by the week 3 deadline; the course guideline says three to four, so the size is being confirmed with the professor

decision: Topic: Smart Urban Living, a Smart Urban Apartment Package for modern multifamily rentals, studied with a choice-based conjoint among renters
rationale: Configurable smart-home technologies and technology-enabled amenities in an otherwise comparable apartment; the question is which features to include and what renters will pay for them

decision: The survey respondent is the renter; the package's buyer is the developer or operator
rationale: Renters, not homebuyers, because rental and purchase decisions carry different financial commitments; the proposal should state both roles in one sentence
source: Proposal v1 and the Sep 16 review

decision: Six attributes: monthly premium, smart access and security, smart climate control, smart lighting, package management, EV charging access
rationale: Features a developer or manager can modify; neighbourhood, size, bedrooms and condition held equal across alternatives. Whether lighting or EV charging survive the pilot, and whether security splits into lock and video, stay open

decision: Price as a monthly premium over a comparable standard apartment, draft levels $0, $25, $50, $75
rationale: The review flags the zero level (a free fully smart package becomes a valid profile) and the missing base-rent anchor; the survey plan locks the levels after the workshop
source: Proposal v1 and the Sep 16 review

decision: Three research questions: which features most influence choice; willingness to pay per feature; which bundle at which premium gives the strongest value proposition
rationale: RQ1 from the relative size of coefficients, RQ2 from coefficient ratios to price, RQ3 from a market simulation of package tiers

decision: Distribution: the proposal names the GWU community and personal and professional networks; the course default is Prolific U.S. general population with an eligibility pre-screen, and the pilot is taken by classmates
rationale: The survey plan (Sep 29) has to state the strategy and the exact eligibility text; the two are reconcilable (Prolific for the final, networks as a supplement) but the plan must say so
source: Proposal v1 and the survey plan page

decision: Two repos: a private brainstorming repo under one member's account, and the official submission repo in the course organisation
rationale: Ideas, decisions and meeting notes stay in the brainstorming repo; every deliverable is pushed from the official repo's numbered folders
To be assigned at the next sync; every member submits at least once

decision: Design parameters: alternatives per choice question, questions per respondent, whether to include a no-choice option
rationale: Needed for the design file (cbc_design) and reported in the pilot analysis; decided when the survey plan is written

decision: Argument for the emerging and pre-commercial criteria: the unresolved design decision is which features to bundle at what premium for mid-market and retrofit stock, and no public source gives tradeoff-based willingness to pay per feature
rationale: To be tested at the proposal workshop; if the professor asks to narrow scope, the fallback is to drop lighting or EV charging or to focus on retrofit packages

decision: Competitor set for the final market simulation: the real products benchmarked in the proposal's attribute table, with their premiums
rationale: The final analysis simulates the package against competitors; the benchmark table written for proposal v2 is the source
